# Sutram

> One set of commands for your web app: people type them in a console, AI agents call them as WebMCP tools or from JavaScript. Every part of the app registers its commands the same way, and they run in the user's own session.

Sutram is an npm package (`@d34dman/sutram`, MIT OR GPL-2.0-or-later) and a Drupal module (`drupal/sutram`). An app registers commands: a name, a JSON Schema for the input, annotations, a function. Agents reach them as WebMCP tools, through `Sutram.tools()`, `Sutram.call()` and `Sutram.exec()` in the page, or as command lines typed into the page's console. `Sutram.agentPrompt()` hands a task to an agent that drives a browser.

Sutram sits on top of WebMCP: WebMCP is how a page hands tools to an agent, and Sutram decides what those tools are. It is one registry that every part of an app (a form, the navigation, a module) registers its commands with, so they are named and found the same way, and people can use the same commands in the console. Sutram registers tools through WebMCP's own `registerTool()` and never reads or changes the page's HTML. It does not replace Playwright or browser agents: they call its commands instead of clicking. Without WebMCP in the browser, the same commands work through `Sutram.call()`.

Agents using a page: start with `status` (or the `sutram_status` tool), then `help`; read `man <command>` before using a command; change one thing per command; ask the person when a call returns exit 130. Coding agents adding Sutram to an app: read the quick start, then Write a provider and Write descriptions agents can use.

## Get started

- [Documentation](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/index.md): Sutram lets AI agents use your web app through commands. Start here.
- [Quick start](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/quick-start.md): Register one command, use it in the console, and call it the way an agent does.
- [Install](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/install.md): Load Sutram as one script, install it from npm, or use the Drupal module.
- [Drupal](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/drupal.md): The drupal/sutram module, its demo submodules, and how a Drupal module adds commands.

## Build commands

- [Write a provider](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/write-a-provider.md): Build a small set of commands step by step, the way the coffee shop on the website does.
- [Nav kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/nav-kit.md): Ready-made nav commands for any app. You write a small adapter that supplies the menus and goes to a URL.
- [Page kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/page-kit.md): page status, the same on every site. Your adapter says what the page is; the kit answers.
- [User kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/user-kit.md): user status, user login and user logout, the same on every site. Your adapter says who is logged in and opens your own login.
- [Messages kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/messages-kit.md): What the page said, such as Saved or an error, as messages status and as message.shown events.
- [Lists kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/lists-kit.md): listing status, listing rows and listing go, the same on every site. Read listings, page through them, sort and filter them.
- [Forms kit](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/forms-kit.md): form list, status, fields, get, set, submit and discard, the same on every site, with add, remove, search and upload where the app has them.
- [Commands and providers](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/commands.md): What a command definition holds, who owns it, and when to register and remove it.
- [Write descriptions agents can use](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/descriptions.md): The documentation agents read is your command definitions. How to write them.
- [Errors that help agents](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/errors.md): How to word failures so an agent fixes one thing instead of starting over.
- [Annotations and the policy](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/annotations-and-policy.md): How commands describe what they do, and how the page decides who has to agree before one runs.
- [Test with Playwright](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/testing.md): Drive a page's commands from a headless browser, in tests or in an agent, with Sutram.tools(), Sutram.call() and Sutram.exec().

## How agents reach them

- [WebMCP](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/webmcp.md): What agents see when Sutram registers your commands as WebMCP tools, and how approval works.
- [The console](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/console.md): Open, use, place, restyle and translate the console that people and pasted command lines use.
- [Hand a task to a browser agent](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/agent-prompt.md): One generic prompt, agentPrompt(), that sends an agent with a browser to the page's console.
- [Discovery: help, man, status](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/discovery.md): How people and agents find out what a page can do and what state it is in.

## Going further

- [Forms](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/forms.md): Field-level commands for forms, progressive disclosure, and validation errors agents can fix.
- [Drafts and saving](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/guides/drafts-and-saving.md): The convention for providers that keep a working copy: status, save, discard.
- [Batches](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/batches.md): Several commands as one change, checked first, asked once, rolled back on failure.
- [Results and exit codes](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/results.md): What every run returns, how the console shows it, and the options every command gets for free.
- [Formats](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/formats.md): App-defined formats such as money, following JSON Schema custom formats.
- [Events](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/concepts/events.md): Facts a page declares and emits, and how agents wait or poll for what changed.

## Reference

- [API](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/reference/api.md): Every export of every entry point, from the TypeScript declarations that ship with the package.
- [The command line](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/reference/command-line.md): Grammar, options, quoting, exit codes, annotations and the words clients own.

## About

- [Why commands](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/why.md): Why agents do better with a standard command interface than with screenshots, page snapshots or one big JSON schema.
- [Measurements](https://d34dman.github.io/sutram/docs/measurements.md): How many tokens an agent spends filling a real Drupal form with and without Sutram, including a correction.
